Diego / Karthik — engineering take below. I ran this against our recent benchmarking and ClearWave's workload pattern. Key assumptions:
- Model family: medium-chat (approx Redwood-medium performance profile)
- Average request: 420 tokens (round-trip) -> average per-request generation 220 tokens outbound
- GPU type: A100-equivalent for throughput estimates (we'll map to customer's preferred sku in the billing sheet)
- Warm cache / prefix reuse is expected to remain in place (we assumed 30% effective latency reduction for common prompts)

Sizing rationale:
- Current steady 260 QPS -> projected steady ~550 QPS (2.1x).
- On our runtime, a single A100-equivalent provides ~45 QPS for this model + token mix when using per-request batching and KV cache.
- To hit 99th-pctl latency targets at steady 550 QPS, required reserved GPUs = ceil(550 / 45) = 13 GPUs.
- Add 15% operational buffer for autoscaling headroom / long-tail requests -> recommended reserved = 15 GPUs.
- Spike/burst plan: keep a dedicated 4-GPU burst pool (pre-warmed) that can be routed for short windows; this covers the 95th-percentile spikes up to ~180 QPS additional. With routing rules, bursts will be limited to 30 minutes per hour before soft overage billing applies.

Proposed SLA structure (high level):
- Throughput SLA: 99.5% of requests below 1.2x baseline latency for sustained load up to 500 QPS on reserved pool.
- Reservation guarantee: capacity for sustained 500 QPS; additional steady-state above 500 QPS handled via ramping pricing or recommending larger reservation.
- Burst handling: pre-warmed burst pool covers short spikes; longer spikes will incur overage at agreed rate (e.g., per-GPU-hour).

Recommendation summary (Customer-facing options):
Option A (Recommended, conservative): 15 reserved GPUs + 4 GPU burst pool (total committed 19). Guaranteed sustained throughput up to 500 QPS; pricing includes a 10% discount for 12-month commitment.
Option B (Cost-efficient): 12 reserved GPUs + 4 GPU burst pool (total 16). Sustained guarantee up to ~420–450 QPS; lower cost but tighter headroom.

I can produce the small SOW snippet that spells out token assumptions, warm cache behavior, and overage rules.

—Monica
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
